mainTopic: Deriving the לא תעשה from ״לאמר״, keeping מצה dough from becoming חמץ, and the opening of אלו עוברין on grain mixtures
overview: The amud opens by showing that the view under discussion is רבי יהודה's. A ברייתא learns that consecrating תמימים for בדק הבית violates an עשה, and adds a לא תעשה from the word ״לאמר״. בר קפרא reads ״לאמר״ as ״לא אמור״, and בי רב read it as ״לאו אמור״. The גמרא then resolves two ברייתות about pouring out a baker's water: a large amount that pools is forbidden, and a small amount that soaks in is allowed. Next come the rules for keeping מצה dough cool: רב יהודה's מים שלנו, with a funny story about how people misunderstood it, and רבא's list of precautions. מר זוטרא and רב אשי disagree about dough kneaded against these rules, and רב אשי rejects מר זוטרא's proof from soaked barley. The chapter כל שעה ends, and the chapter אלו עוברין opens with a משנה listing grain-containing products that carry an אזהרה but no כרת. The גמרא then brings ברייתות about the health effects of כותח and other foods, and begins to define פת נקייה, a definition that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The opinion belongs to רבי יהודה, as shown by a ברייתא on blemished animals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the opinion under discussion is רבי יהודה's. It cites a ברייתא: a בעל מום may be consecrated for בדק הבית, but consecrating תמימים for בדק הבית violates an עשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is רבי יהודה's view, as a ברייתא teaches: "A bull or a lamb with a limb too long or too short, you may make it a free-will offering." This means you may consecrate *it* (the blemished animal) for Temple maintenance, but you may not consecrate unblemished animals for Temple maintenance. From here they said: anyone who consecrates unblemished animals for Temple maintenance transgresses a positive command.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us whose opinion we are dealing with, namely רבי יהודה's. It then quotes a ברייתא to show where his view comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says a blemished animal may be given as a נדבה, meaning donated to בדק הבית. The word ״אותו״ ("it") limits this to the blemished animal, so an unblemished animal, which is fit for the מזבח, may not be diverted to בדק הבית. Because this prohibition is only implied by a positive statement, at this stage it counts as an עשה.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught (in a ברייתא)
An animal with a limb too long / too short (a type of blemish)
Consecrates (designates something as holy)
The Temple maintenance fund
Unblemished animals, fit for the מזבח
Transgresses a positive command

steps.confusionAlert: ״נדבה תעשה אותו״ here does NOT mean offering it on the מזבח. A blemished animal cannot be sacrificed. It means donating it to בדק הבית.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Yehuda,
as it was taught in a baraita:
"A bull or a lamb with a limb too long or too short,
you may make it a free-will offering."
It (the blemished one) you may consecrate for Temple maintenance,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אַתָּה מַתְפִּיס תְּמִימִים לְבֶדֶק הַבַּיִת.
phrases.english: but you may not consecrate unblemished animals for Temple maintenance.
From here they said:
Whoever consecrates unblemished animals for Temple maintenance
transgresses a positive command.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the author of the opinion discussed on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Consecrating תמימים for בדק הבית violates an עשה, derived from ״אותו״ in the פסוק.

steps.title: Is there also a negative prohibition?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks: so far we have only an עשה. Where do we learn that there is also a לא תעשה?
steps.simpleTranslation: So far I have only a positive command. From where do I know there is also a prohibition?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a follow-up question and sets up the next step. It wants to know whether this act also breaks a לא תעשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 produced only an implied עשה. The ברייתא now looks for a stronger source that turns this into a full לא תעשה.

keyTerms.meaning: I have only (so far we know only)
A negative prohibition
From where (do we know)?

phrases.english: I have only a positive command;
from where do I know a prohibition?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא בַּעֲשֵׂה, בְּלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the עשה from step 1 by asking about a לא תעשה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that consecrating תמימים for בדק הבית is also a לא תעשה.

steps.title: The opening verse makes the whole portion a prohibition
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה learns from ״וידבר ה׳ אל משה לאמר״ that the entire פרשה carries a לא תעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: "And ה׳ spoke to משה, saying." This teaches about the entire portion that it is under a prohibition. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question by pointing to the opening line of the פרשה. According to רבי יהודה, that line places every law in the section under a לא תעשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה does not need a separate ״לא״ for each law. The introductory line covers all of them at once, so even laws that sound positive, like our case, also count as a לא תעשה.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches
It taught regarding
A Torah portion/section
The words (opinion) of

steps.whyThisMatters: This is why the גמרא linked the earlier opinion to רבי יהודה. He holds that a law phrased positively can still carry the force of a לא תעשה.

phrases.english: The verse states:
"And ה׳ spoke to Moshe, saying"
this teaches about the entire portion
that it should be under a prohibition;
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: וַיְדַבֵּר ה׳ אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The introductory phrase ״וידבר ה׳ אל משה לאמר״ makes the entire פרשה a לא תעשה, according to רבי יהודה.

steps.title: רבי asks how the verse implies this
steps.stepSummary: רבי asks בר קפרא how the opening verse implies a לא תעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said to בר קפרא: What in the verse implies this?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי asks בר קפרא to explain how רבי יהודה reads a prohibition into the opening line. This sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״וידבר ה׳ אל משה לאמר״ is a standard introduction that appears many times and does not obviously mean "prohibition." רבי wants the precise textual hook.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי, meaning רבי יהודה הנשיא
בר קפרא, a student of רבי
What is the implication? (How is this derived?)

steps.confusionAlert: ״רבי״ here is רבי יהודה הנשיא, the compiler of the משנה. He is not the same person as רבי יהודה (בר אילעאי), whose opinion is being explained.

phrases.english: Rebbi said to Bar Kappara:
What is the implication?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי לְבַר קַפָּרָא: מַאי מַשְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the mechanism behind the derivation in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which word in ״וידבר ה׳ אל משה לאמר״ signals a לא תעשה.

steps.title: ״לאמר״ is read as ״לא אמור״
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא explains that ״לאמר״ is read as ״לא אמור״, so the word ״לא″ is said about all the matters that follow.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Because it is written ״לאמר״, which hints that ״לא″ ("no") is said about these matters.
steps.whatsHappening: בר קפרא answers by reading the word ״לאמר״ as if it contains ״לא״. This makes every law in the section a prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״לאמר״ begins with the letters ל־א, which spell ״לא״. רבי יהודה treats this as a hidden "no" placed on all the laws in the פרשה. That hidden "no" is the source of the לא תעשה, including for consecrating תמימים for בדק הבית.

keyTerms.meaning: For it is written
"Saying", here read as ״לא אמור״ ("no" is said)
Regarding the matters (the laws that follow)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, consecrating תמימים for בדק הבית violates both an עשה (from ״אותו״) and a לא תעשה (from ״לאמר״, read as ״לא אמור״).

phrases.english: He said to him:
For it is written "leimor" (saying):
"no" is stated regarding these matters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי's question from step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״לאמר״ is expounded as ״לא אמור״, placing a לא תעשה on the whole פרשה.

steps.title: The school of רב reads 'saying' as 'say a prohibition'
steps.stepSummary: בי רב give their own way of finding a לא תעשה in the word ״לאמר״: read it as ״לאו אמור״, meaning 'say a prohibition.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רב say: the word 'saying' (לאמר) should be read as 'say a לאו' (a prohibition).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to how ״לאמר״ teaches a לא תעשה. This one comes from בי רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 5, בר קפרא read ״לאמר״ as ״לא אמור״, meaning the word 'not' is said about everything that follows. בי רב read it as ״לאו אמור״, meaning משה is told to say a prohibition. Both readings arrive at the same result: the מצוות in this פרשה carry a לא תעשה.

keyTerms.meaning: The school, or study hall, of רב
A negative commandment, a prohibition
Say! (a command)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two readings of ״לאמר״. בר קפרא says ״לא אמור״ (the word 'not' is said here). בי רב says ״לאו אמור״ (say a prohibition). Both conclude that this פרשה contains a לא תעשה.

phrases.english: The school of Rav say:
'Saying' means: say a prohibition.
phrases.notes: A wordplay: לאמר is split into לאו + אמור.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different reading of the same word that בר קפרא explained in Step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How does ״לאמר״ show that there is a לא תעשה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Read ״לאמר״ as ״לאו אמור״: say a prohibition.

steps.title: Two ברייתות disagree about pouring a baker's water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה about a baker's used water. One ברייתא says it may be poured only on a slope. Another ברייתא allows it even where water collects.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'A baker's used water must be poured out.' One ברייתא teaches: you may pour it on a sloped place, but not in a place where water gathers. Another ברייתא teaches: you may pour it even in a place where water gathers!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה. It points out that two ברייתות seem to contradict each other about where the baker's water may be poured.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A baker's water has bits of dough in it, which can become חמץ. On a slope, the water runs off and soaks in fast. Where water collects, it sits, and the dough might rise. The first ברייתא forbids that kind of spot, and the second permits it, so they look like they clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Its used water: water the baker used to cool his hands or wash utensils
A baker
A slope, a sloped place
A level place where water collects and pools
It was taught in another ברייתא (introduces a contradicting source)

phrases.english: We learned in the mishna: Water used by a baker, etc.
phrases.notes: Quotes the משנה to introduce the new topic.

phrases.english: It was taught in one baraita:
One may pour it out in a sloped place,
but one may not pour it out in a place where water collects.
And it was taught in another baraita:
One may pour it out in a place where water collects!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. The גמרא returns to the next line of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: How the two ברייתות fit together on pouring a baker's water
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One ברייתא forbids pouring where water collects, and the other permits it. Both cannot be right as they stand.

steps.title: A lot of water versus a little water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the forbidding ברייתא speaks about a large amount of water that pools. The permitting ברייתא speaks about a small amount that does not pool.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This ברייתא, which forbids, is about a lot of water, which collects in one spot. That ברייתא, which permits, is about a little water, which does not collect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction from Step 7. It shows that each ברייתא is talking about a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lot of water sits in a puddle, so the dough in it can rise and become חמץ. That is why it is forbidden. A little water soaks into the ground before the dough can rise, so it is allowed. The ברייתות do not really disagree; they are describing different amounts of water.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (introduces a resolution)
They are many: a large amount
They collect, pool, gather together

steps.whatToRemember: A baker's water may not be poured where it will pool if there is a lot of it. A small amount, which soaks in quickly, may be poured even on level ground.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
This one is about a large amount, which collects.
That one is about a small amount, which does not collect.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction from Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each ברייתא is about a different amount of water
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות disagree about pouring where water collects.
steps.terutzMaskana: A lot of water that pools is forbidden. A little water that soaks in is allowed.

steps.title: Knead מצה only with water that sat overnight
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that a woman may knead מצה dough only with מים שלנו: water that was left overnight to cool.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: a woman may knead מצה dough only with water that has rested overnight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רב יהודה about what kind of water to use for מצה dough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water that was just drawn is still a little warm, and warm water makes dough rise faster. Water that sat overnight has cooled down. Cool water slows the rising, which protects the מצה from becoming חמץ.

keyTerms.meaning: Knead (dough)
Water that stayed overnight (from the word לָן, to stay the night)
Unleavened bread

steps.confusionAlert: מים שלנו does NOT mean 'our water.' It comes from לָן, to stay overnight. It means water that was left overnight to cool.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the הלכה of מים שלנו, which is still kept today when baking מצה.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
A woman may not knead
except with water that rested overnight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling. It stays on the theme of preventing water from making dough into חמץ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מצה dough may be kneaded only with water that was left overnight to cool.

steps.title: The people misunderstand רב מתנה's rule about water
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנה taught the rule of מים שלנו in פפוניא. The next day everyone came to him with jugs asking for water, because they thought it meant 'our water.' He explained he meant water that rested overnight.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מתנה taught this rule in פפוניא. The next day everyone brought their jugs to him and said, 'Give us water!' He told them: 'I meant water that rested overnight.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short, funny story about how people misunderstood רב יהודה's rule of מים שלנו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words מים שלנו can sound like 'water that stayed overnight' (from the root לין) or like 'our water' (from שלנו = ours). The people thought the rabbi meant they must take his water, so he explained it in Aramaic: מיא דביתו, water that rested overnight. The story makes clear that the rule is about the water being cool, not about whose water it is.

keyTerms.meaning: He taught it publicly
Their jugs
Water that rested overnight
The name of a town

steps.confusionAlert: שלנו here does NOT mean 'ours.' It comes from לָן, 'stayed overnight.' That is exactly the mistake the people in the story made.

phrases.english: Rav Mattana taught it publicly in Paphunya.
phrases.notes: 'It' refers to רב יהודה's rule of מים שלנו

phrases.english: The next day, everyone brought their jugs
and came to him, and said to him:
Give us water.
phrases.notes: They thought שלנו meant 'ours,' meaning the rabbi's water

phrases.english: He said to them:
I was speaking about water that rested overnight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that explains the meaning of the words in רב יהודה's rule from step 9
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מים שלנו means water that rested overnight, not 'our water.'

steps.title: רבא lists more precautions for kneading מצה
steps.stepSummary: רבא teaches that a woman may not knead מצה in the sun, with sun-heated water, or with water taken from a heated urn. She must keep working until all the dough is baked, and she needs two vessels of water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא taught: A woman may not knead in the sun, nor with water warmed by the sun, nor with water taken from a heated urn. She may not stop working at the oven until she finishes all the bread. She needs two vessels: one for wetting the dough and one for cooling her hands.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a list of practical rules that keep the dough cool and keep the work moving, so it does not become חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Heat makes dough rise faster, so every heat source is avoided: the sun, sun-warmed water, and water from a heated urn. Stopping in the middle gives the dough time to rise, so she must keep going. Her warm hands can also heat the dough, so she keeps a separate vessel of water to cool them.

keyTerms.meaning: To knead dough
Water heated by the sun
An urn heated by coals
Wetting or smoothing the dough with water
Cooling down

steps.whyThisMatters: These rules are the basis for the practical care taken when baking מצה today: keeping water and dough cool and working without stopping.

phrases.english: Rava taught publicly:
A woman may not knead in the sun,
nor with water heated by the sun,
nor with water drawn from a coal-heated urn,
and she may not lift her hand from the oven
phrases.notes: Meaning she may not take a break in the middle

phrases.english: until she finishes all the bread.
And she needs two vessels:
one that she uses to wet the dough,
and one that she uses to cool her hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more precautions alongside רב יהודה's rule of מים שלנו
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Avoid every source of heat and every delay when kneading and baking מצה.

steps.title: What if she broke the rules and kneaded anyway?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the law is, after the fact, if a woman kneaded against these rules, for example with warm water.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: If she broke the rule and kneaded anyway, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question that sets up the next step: are these rules only for the start, or is the dough forbidden if she broke them?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, the rules told us what to do from the start (לכתחילה). Now the question is about after the fact (בדיעבד): is dough made with warm water automatically forbidden, or only if it actually became חמץ?

keyTerms.meaning: It was asked of them; a question the scholars were unsure about
She transgressed, meaning she broke the rule
What is the law?

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
If she broke the rule and kneaded, what is the law?
phrases.notes: For example, she kneaded with warm water instead of מים שלנו

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the after-the-fact result of breaking the rules from steps 9 and 11
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is dough kneaded against these rules forbidden after the fact?

steps.title: מר זוטרא permits and רב אשי forbids
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא says the dough is permitted after the fact. רב אשי says it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: It is permitted. רב אשי said: It is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give opposite answers to the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר זוטרא holds that the rules are only extra caution, so if the dough did not actually become חמץ, it may be eaten. רב אשי holds that warm water makes the dough treated as forbidden even if we cannot see any rising.

keyTerms.meaning: Permitted
Forbidden

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said: It is permitted,
Rav Ashi said: It is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives two opposing answers to the question in step 12
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מר זוטרא: permitted after the fact. רב אשי: forbidden.

steps.title: מר זוטרא's proof from soaking barley
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא brings a ברייתא: one may not soak barley on פסח, but if he did, the barley is forbidden only if the grains split. This shows that breaking the rule alone does not forbid the food.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: How do I know this? Because a ברייתא teaches: One may not soak barley on פסח. If he soaked it anyway, then if the grains split, they are forbidden; if they did not split, they are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא supports his view that the dough is permitted with a ברייתא about soaking barley.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Soaking barley is forbidden from the start, just like kneading with warm water. Yet the ברייתא forbids the barley after the fact only if it actually split, which is a sign of becoming חמץ. So too, dough kneaded against the rules is forbidden only if it actually became חמץ.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say this? (introduces a proof)
As it was taught in a ברייתא
Soaking grain in water
They split, a sign of becoming חמץ

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said:
From where do I say this?
As it was taught in a ברייתא:
One may not soak barley on Pesach.
And if he did soak it,
if the grains split, they are forbidden;
if they did not split, they are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: מר זוטרא brings support for his ruling from step 13
steps.raayaObject: מר זוטרא's ruling that dough kneaded against the rules is permitted after the fact
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: soaked barley is forbidden only if the grains split
steps.whatToRemember: Breaking a precaution from the start does not automatically forbid the food. According to מר זוטרא, it is forbidden only if it actually became חמץ, just as soaked barley is forbidden only when it splits.

steps.title: רב אשי: not every rule works the same way
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rejects מר זוטרא's proof. The barley case does not teach us about warm-water dough, because each rabbinic rule has its own law.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב אשי said: Do you think all these rules were woven from one piece of cloth? Where the חכמים said the food stays permitted after the fact, they said it. Where they did not say it, they did not say it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי pushes back against the proof that מר זוטרא brought from the barley ברייתא. He says you cannot copy the outcome of one rule onto a different rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר זוטרא argued that breaking a rabbinic rule does not forbid the food, just as with the barley. רב אשי answers that the ברייתא only tells us the result for barley. For warm-water dough, the חכמים may have forbidden the food after the fact as a penalty, so רב אשי's ruling of forbidden still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say...? (introduces a rhetorical challenge)
They were all woven in one weaving, meaning they all follow the same rule
Where it was stated
After the fact (once it already happened)

steps.whatToRemember: מר זוטרא says dough kneaded against the rules is permitted after the fact. רב אשי says it is forbidden, because each rule has its own outcome and the barley case cannot be copied over.
steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not saying the barley ברייתא is wrong. He agrees the barley is permitted unless the grains split. He only denies that this proves anything about dough kneaded with warm water.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches an important principle: one rabbinic decree's after-the-fact leniency cannot automatically be applied to a different decree.

phrases.english: And Rav Ashi said:
Is that to say that all of them
were woven in one single weaving?!
phrases.notes: A picture: these rules are not one piece of cloth that all share the same pattern.

phrases.english: Where it was stated, it was stated,
phrases.notes: Where the חכמים said the food is permitted after the fact, it is permitted.

phrases.english: and where it was not stated, it was not stated.
phrases.notes: Where they did not say so, we cannot assume it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: אַטּוּ כּוּלְּהוּ חֲדָא מְחִיתָא מְחִיתִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought by מר זוטרא in step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not reject the barley law itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof wrongly assumes that all rabbinic kneading and soaking rules share the same after-the-fact outcome.

steps.title: הדרן: closing the chapter כל שעה
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the second chapter of פסחים, כל שעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter כל שעה.
steps.whatsHappening: The chapter כל שעה ends here. The line is a traditional farewell said at the end of every chapter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is argued here. It marks a boundary: the discussion about eating and benefiting from חמץ, and about making מצה, is finished. A new chapter is about to begin.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (said when finishing a chapter)
כל שעה, the name of the second chapter of פסחים

phrases.english: We will return to you, chapter Kol Sha'ah

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after רב אשי's final word.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter כל שעה is complete.

steps.title: משנה: list of grain mixtures one may not keep on פסח
steps.stepSummary: The new chapter opens with a list of foods and products containing חמץ grain. Owning them violates בל יראה and בל ימצא.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: For these things, one transgresses on פסח: Babylonian כותח, Median beer, Edomite vinegar, Egyptian זיתום, dyers' broth, cooks' starch dough, and scribes' glue.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins the chapter אלו עוברין. It lists seven items that are not plain bread but contain חמץ grain, and says owning them on פסח is a violation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that even mixtures, and even non-food products like dye or glue, count when they contain חמץ grain. The word עוברין means one breaks the prohibitions against owning חמץ: בל יראה and בל ימצא.

keyTerms.meaning: One transgresses, here meaning violating בל יראה and בל ימצא
A sharp dip made with bread crusts, whey and salt
An Egyptian drink made with barley
Bran water used by dyers
Flour paste or starch dough
Glue, here the glue used by scribes

steps.confusionAlert: עוברין here does not mean 'passing' or 'crossing over.' It means 'transgressing,' that is, breaking the prohibition of owning חמץ.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the chapter's main topic: חמץ that is mixed into other things (תערובת חמץ), or that is not ordinary food.

phrases.english: MISHNA: And for these, one transgresses on Pesach:
Babylonian kutach, and Median beer,
and Edomite vinegar, and Egyptian zitom,
and the bran-water broth of dyers,
and the starch dough of cooks,
and the glue of scribes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new chapter after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Owning these seven grain-containing products on פסח violates the prohibition of owning חמץ.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר adds women's cosmetics
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר adds women's cosmetics that contain grain to the list of forbidden items.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: Also women's cosmetics.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר adds one more item to the משנה's list: women's cosmetics made with grain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These cosmetics are clearly not food, yet רבי אליעזר holds that owning them still violates the prohibition of owning חמץ. This shows he extends the rule even further toward non-edible products.

keyTerms.meaning: Women's adornments, here meaning cosmetics made with flour
Also, even

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
Also women's cosmetics.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אַף תַּכְשִׁיטֵי נָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an item to the list given in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Women's cosmetics that contain grain are also included in the prohibition.

steps.title: The general rule: anything made from grain is included
steps.stepSummary: The משנה sums up its list with one rule. Any item that contains a type of grain is included in the prohibition on פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the general rule: anything that comes from a type of grain, a person transgresses with it on פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes its list of foods and products with one general principle. The principle tells us what all the items on the list have in common.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list was not meant to be complete. Any product that contains one of the five grains (דגן) is included, even if it is not named in the list. Owning such a product on פסח violates the prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the general rule. It is used to sum up a list of cases.
A type of grain, meaning the five grains that can become חמץ.
Transgresses, meaning one violates the prohibition.

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule turns a list of specific examples into a guideline that can be applied to new products.

phrases.aramaic: זֶה הַכְּלָל: כׇּל שֶׁהוּא מִמִּין דָּגָן —
phrases.english: This is the general rule: anything that is from a type of grain —
one transgresses with it on Pesach.
phrases.notes: This refers to the prohibitions of בל יראה and בל ימצא mentioned at the start of the משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה הַכְּלָל: כׇּל שֶׁהוּא מִמִּין דָּגָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the list in steps 17 and 18 with a general principle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any product containing grain is included in the prohibition on פסח.

steps.title: A warning but no כרת
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states the level of the prohibition. These items carry an אזהרה (a warning), but not the punishment of כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: These items are under a warning, but they do not carry the punishment of כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells us how serious the prohibition on these items is. It is a real prohibition, but it is not punished with כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating pure, full חמץ on פסח carries כרת. The items on this list are not pure, full חמץ, so their law is lighter. They are still forbidden, but they do not carry כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: A warning, meaning a prohibition.
Spiritual cutting off, the severe punishment for eating real חמץ on פסח.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think these items are permitted. They are forbidden. The only difference is that the punishment is less severe than for pure חמץ.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's list = products containing grain. They are forbidden on פסח with an אזהרה, but they carry no כרת.

phrases.english: These are under a warning,
but they do not carry the punishment of karet.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ בָּאַזְהָרָה, וְאֵין בָּהֶן מִשּׁוּם כָּרֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the level of punishment to the general rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The listed items are forbidden with an אזהרה, but they carry no כרת.

steps.title: Three harmful effects of כותח הבבלי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by quoting a ברייתא. It says כותח הבבלי, which was the first item on the משנה's list, has three harmful effects on the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: three things were said about Babylonian כותח. It blocks the heart, it blinds the eyes, and it weakens the body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. Because the משנה mentioned כותח, the גמרא brings a ברייתא about its harmful effects.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a legal discussion. It is health information connected to a food named in the משנה. The ברייתא lists three bad effects, and the next step explains the cause of each one.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught. This introduces a ברייתא.
Babylonian כותח, a dip made from whey, salt, and moldy bread crumbs.
Blocks the heart, meaning it dulls a person's understanding.
Weakens.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught,
three things were said about Babylonian kutach:
it blocks the heart,
and it blinds the eyes,
and it weakens the body.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן, שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים נֶאֱמָרִים בְּכוּתָּח הַבַּבְלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא with a ברייתא about כותח, an item from the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כותח הבבלי blocks the heart, blinds the eyes, and weakens the body.

steps.title: The cause of each harmful effect
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains which ingredient of כותח causes each harmful effect: the whey, the salt, and the moldy bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: It blocks the heart because of the milk whey. It blinds the eyes because of the salt. It weakens the body because of the moldy bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back through the three effects from the ברייתא. For each one, it names the ingredient that causes it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each harm is linked to one of the three ingredients of כותח. The whey dulls the heart, the salt harms the eyes, and the moldy bread crumbs weaken the body. The moldy bread is the grain part, which is why כותח is on the חמץ list in the first place.

keyTerms.meaning: Milk whey, the watery part left over from milk.
Salt.
Moldy bread, meaning bread crumbs that leavened until they were nearly spoiled.
Because of.

phrases.aramaic: מְטַמְטֵם אֶת הַלֵּב — מִשּׁוּם נַסְיוּבֵי דַחֲלָבָא.
phrases.english: It blocks the heart — because of the milk whey.
And it blinds the eyes — because of the salt.

phrases.aramaic: וּמַכְחִישׁ אֶת הַגּוּף — מִשּׁוּם קוֹמָנִיתָא דְאוּמָא.
phrases.english: And it weakens the body — because of the moldy bread.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְטַמְטֵם אֶת הַלֵּב — מִשּׁוּם נַסְיוּבֵי דַחֲלָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the cause of each of the three effects listed in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each harm of כותח comes from a specific ingredient: the whey, the salt, or the moldy bread.

steps.title: Three foods that harm a person's health
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא continues with another ברייתא about health. It lists three foods that increase waste, lower a person's height, and weaken eyesight: coarse bread, new beer, and raw vegetables.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: three things increase waste, bend a person's height, and take away one five-hundredth of a person's eyesight. They are coarse bread, new beer, and raw vegetables.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that it has discussed a harmful food, the גמרא brings a related ברייתא about other foods that harm a person's health.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This step leaves the משנה's list behind and continues the topic of health. Like the first ברייתא, it uses a pattern of three. Here there are three harms and three foods that cause them.

keyTerms.meaning: Waste, meaning bodily excrement.
Height or stature.
Eyesight.
Bread made from coarse flour that still contains bran.
New beer that has not yet aged.
Raw vegetables.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
three things increase waste,
and bend the stature,
and take away one five-hundredth
of a person's eyesight,
and they are: coarse bread,
and new beer, and raw vegetables.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים מַרְבִּין הַזֶּבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the health topic with a second ברייתא built on a similar pattern of three.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Coarse bread, new beer, and raw vegetables increase waste, lower a person's stature, and weaken eyesight.

steps.title: Three foods that are good for the body
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists three foods that reduce waste, help a person stand tall, and brighten the eyes: fine bread, fatty meat, and aged wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Three things reduce waste, make a person stand tall, and brighten the eyes. They are fine bread, fatty meat, and aged wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new ברייתא that lists three healthy foods. It is the opposite of the ברייתא we just learned about three harmful foods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous ברייתא (Step 23) said coarse bread, new beer, and raw vegetables increase waste, lower height, and weaken eyesight. This ברייתא lists the reverse effects: less waste, standing tall, and brighter eyes. The foods are reversed too: fine bread instead of coarse bread, and aged wine instead of new beer.

keyTerms.meaning: Reduce bodily waste
Make a person stand upright and tall
Brighten the eyes and improve eyesight
Fatty meat
Old, aged wine

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a הלכה about פסח. The גמרא is continuing a run of health teachings that started with כותח הבבלי. These ברייתות are grouped together because they share the same 'three things' pattern.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Three things reduce waste,
phrases.notes: The opposite of 'increase waste' in the previous ברייתא.

phrases.english: and make a person stand tall,
phrases.notes: The opposite of 'lower a person's height.'

phrases.english: and brighten the eyes.
These are: fine bread,
fatty meat, and aged wine.
phrases.notes: Aged wine stands in contrast to new beer.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים מְמַעֲטִין אֶת הַזֶּבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the mirror image of Step 23. It lists the foods with the opposite, beneficial effects.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fine bread, fatty meat, and aged wine reduce waste, help a person stand tall, and brighten the eyes.

steps.title: Starting to explain what fine bread means
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא picks up the first item of the ברייתא, פת נקייה, so that it can define it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fine bread:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It repeats the first item, פת נקייה, so that it can explain exactly what kind of bread this means. The explanation comes in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Quoting a term and then defining it is a common pattern in the גמרא. It did the same thing with כותח in Step 22, when it explained which ingredient caused each effect. Here the open question is what makes bread count as 'fine.'

keyTerms.meaning: Fine bread, made from well-sifted flour
Clean or refined, meaning the bran has been sifted out
Bread

phrases.english: Fine bread:
phrases.notes: Setup line. The definition follows on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It picks up the first food in the list from Step 24 so the גמרא can define it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The גמרא begins to define the term פת נקייה; the definition itself comes next.
